task.name: A working tree survives the story-text change that invalidated the phases which produced it, so a dev inherits superseded work as its starting point
task.story_text:
## Observed

Phase records produced against a story's earlier text are discarded when that text changes, but
the working tree those phases produced is carried into the new run unexamined.

A story was stopped mid-DEV with uncommitted work in its worktree. Its issue body was then
corrected — the diagnosis it had been implementing named the wrong mechanism. On the next run,
recovery correctly refused the recorded phases:

```
if recorded_hash != story_content_hash(story_content):
    return False, "story_content_changed"
```

No phase was recovered and the run replanned from preflight, which is the right response to a
story whose text no longer matches what was planned. The worktree received no such treatment:

```
⚠ WORKSPACE  existing worktree found: .../issue-2284
↻ WORKSPACE  reusing existing worktree: .../issue-2284
```

The new dev agent therefore began against a tree containing an implementation of the superseded
diagnosis — 260 lines that the corrected text explicitly rules out — and spent part of its first
iteration reverting it before doing its own work. The reverted approach had removed a constant
the corrected text depends on; the constant is present again in the landed result, so the revert
was real work with no product.

The same two lines appear on a run started without resume, so this is not resume-specific: any
run finding an existing worktree adopts whatever it contains, regardless of whether the story
text that produced it still governs.

## Expected

Recovering prior work and recovering prior phase records are the same judgement about the same
question — whether what an earlier attempt produced was produced against the story that is being
run now. Applying that judgement to the records and not to the artifacts leaves the cheaper half
of the evidence guarded and the expensive half unguarded, and the failure is quiet: a working
tree carries no provenance an agent can read, so a dev inherits a superseded implementation as
though it were its own starting point.

Discarding the work is not automatically right — a stopped story's tree is often exactly what
should continue, and deleting it on a wording change would be worse than the present behaviour.
What is missing is that the question is asked at all. Where an earlier attempt's output is
carried into a run whose story text has changed, that fact belongs where both the operator and
the agent can see it, so continuing is a decision rather than a default.

An operator who edits an issue while its story is stopped has changed what the work should be. It
is reasonable for the system to keep the work and reasonable for it to set it aside; it is not
reasonable for the choice to depend on which of two artifacts happens to carry a content hash.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** after a story's text changes, a new run discards the recorded phases but
  adopts the previous attempt's working tree, and the dev agent spends effort undoing work the
  new text rules out.
- **Evidence:** `coordinator/resume_persistence.py:383` compares `record["story_content_hash"]`
  against `story_content_hash(story_content)` and returns `story_content_changed`, rejecting
  recovery. Workspace setup has no equivalent check: run `e8340b0c787d` logged `existing worktree
  found` / `reusing existing worktree` for `issue-2284` and no `RESUME recovered phase record`
  line. The adopted tree held the prior run's diff (7 files, 260 insertions, 38 deletions); the
  landed result restores `_ESTIMATE_HEADROOM_BY_BAND`, which that diff had deleted.
- **Ruled out:** not a defect in the content-hash guard, which behaved correctly — the phases
  were planned against text that no longer governed and were rightly discarded.
- **Ruled out:** not resume-specific. The same worktree-reuse lines are emitted on runs started
  without resume, so the gap is in workspace adoption rather than in the resume path.
- **Ruled out:** not a stale-worktree sweep problem. The worktree was current, clean of the
  previous run's process, and belonged to this story; nothing about it was stale except the
  intent behind its contents.
- **Confirmed cause:** the provenance test that governs whether prior phase records may be reused
  is applied only to those records. Workspace setup adopts an existing worktree on identity alone
  and never consults the story text that produced its contents.
- **Affected code path:** the recovery guard in `coordinator.resume_persistence` and the
  worktree-adoption path in workspace setup.
- **Fix-success criterion:** when a run adopts an existing worktree, whether the story text that
  produced its contents still governs is determined and recorded, and where it does not, that is
  surfaced rather than left implicit. A story whose text has not changed continues to reuse its
  worktree exactly as it does now.

handoff.summary: Applied the provenance judgement that governs phase-record recovery to worktree adoption. New coordinator/worktree_provenance.py persists the story-content hash that produced a story's workspace (.forge/worktree_state/<slug>.json, same idiom as resume_state) and evaluates it on every path in _create_workspace that adopts contents an earlier attempt produced — reuse-by-path, reuse-of-registered-worktree, and reattach-branch-with-commits — recording the currently-governing text on every successful exit including fresh creation, and clearing the record when a stale tree is removed. The tree is never discarded on the answer; what changes is that the answer is stated: workspace.py logs a warning block naming both short hashes, engine.py lifts the recorded judgement onto CoordinatorState (workspace_provenance_status / workspace_inherited_work_note) and emits a workspace_provenance event, audit.py records workspace.story_provenance and workspace.inherited_superseded_work (record schema bumped 22→23 with reader-side _migrate_v22_to_v23 backfilling None/False rather than inventing a judgement), and dev_phase.py injects an 'Inherited Working Tree' section into the first dev prompt, consumed after one injection so later iterations are not warned about their own work. A story whose text has not changed reuses its worktree exactly as before — no new log line, no prompt section, no state change. Four statuses are distinguished so a tree predating the record reads as unknown rather than superseded. A run with no story text in hand writes nothing, so it cannot corrupt the next run's comparison.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the P1: the run audit derived workspace.inherited_superseded_work from state.workspace_inherited_work_note, which _run_dev_phase deliberately clears after the first dev prompt carries it — so the field reported false for exactly the runs that inherited superseded work and proceeded into DEV. It is now derived from state.workspace_provenance_status == PROVENANCE_CHANGED, which WORKSPACE writes once and nothing consumes. Because 'the run inherited superseded work' and 'the dev agent was told about it' are separate facts, a sticky state.workspace_inherited_work_surfaced_to_dev is set at injection time (never cleared) and recorded as workspace.inherited_work_surfaced_to_dev, so an audit can still tell a warned dev from a run that stopped before DEV; without it, deriving from status alone would have erased the agent-facing half of the evidence. Both fields backfill False through the existing _migrate_v22_to_v23 helper and the v23 schema snapshot was regenerated — no second version bump, since v23 is introduced by this same unreleased change. The state field carrying the note now documents that it is a one-shot channel nothing may derive a run-level fact from. I swept audit.py, audit_render.py and landing_record.py for other reads of consumed one-shot state (escalation_note, human_feedback, retry_reason) and found none. Iteration-0 code paths were re-checked for collateral effects: workspace.py, engine.py, worktree_provenance.py and dev_prompts.py are unchanged by this fix, and the provenance status they produce was already written once per run at WORKSPACE.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
